To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the tropical SSTs are the dominant cause of the recent weakening of the East Asian summer monsoonal circulation, but the rainfall changes in the subtropics are more difficult to simulate.

the recent tropical SST warming is the main cause for the observed weakening of East Asian summer (monsoon) circulation, and that a realistic simulation of East China rainfall changes remains a challenge for global models.

the tropical SST forcing plays an important role in the recent weakening of the EAS summer monsoon circulation, while the global SST forcing and the greenhouse gases plus aerosol forcing have contributed to the recent strengthening of the EASM rainfall over East China.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the relative roles of different forcing in inducing the decadal variability of the EASM.
the relative roles of the tropical SSTs, global SSTs, and greenhouse gases plus (direct) atmospheric aerosols in causing the observed decadal changes of the EASM.
the role of the tropical Pacific SST in modulating the EASM and its impact on the summer rainfall over East Asia.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the observed weakening of EASM circulation and the associated weakening of summer rainfall in East China during the late 1978–1990s is mainly caused by the tropical warming.
the recent EASM change is mainly caused by the tropical SST forcing, but the global SST and aerosols also play important roles.

both global warming and the tropical SST variability are important in causing the recent weakening of the EAM, and that both factors are needed for a realistic simulation of EAM rainfall changes over the East China region.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the recent warming of the Tropics has caused the weakening of the summer monsoon, while the greenhouse forcing has contributed to the strengthening of the land-sea contrast, which has caused an increase of summer rainfall over East Asia.
the EASM is sensitive to the tropical SSTs and global SSTs, while the rainfall over East China is more sensitive to the tropical than global SSTs.
both the global SSTs and the direct greenhouse gas and aerosol forcings have contributed to the recent changes of the EASM and rainfall over East Asia, but their roles are quite different.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the observed changes of the EASM and summer rainfall over the last 50 yr can be largely explained by the changes of tropical SSTs and global forcing.
the EASM and its associated precipitation are sensitive to the SST forcing, and that global warming may have opposite effects on the monsoon circulation and rainfall over East Asia.

the observed weakening of EASM during the late 1979–2000 period can be largely explained by the observed warming in the Tropic, and that the observed rainfall change pattern is more closely related to the regional SST forcing.
